answer: The geometric structure of the embedding space automatically enforces consistent hierarchical predictions. In order embeddings, a general concept has smaller values than a specific concept in every coordinate, directly enforcing partial-order constraints such as transitivity.

The embedding space itself enforces partial-order constraints and globally consistent predictions. In order embeddings, a general concept’s vector is smaller than a specific concept’s vector in every coordinate, so hierarchical relations such as transitivity follow automatically from the geometry.

Reordering means rearranging words in word-by-word translation outputs to match the word order of the target language.

Reordering means rearranging translated words into the correct order of the target language, since word-by-word translation preserves an unsuitable word order. The denoising autoencoder learns to correct this using training sentences corrupted by random word permutations.
